sources.title: Choose a model: Palmyra X6, X5 and X4 comparison
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27: the exact X4 column and section identify palmyra-x4 and 128k context, with December 14, 2026 deprecation. Neither total nor active parameters, a sized base checkpoint, or network structure is disclosed. X5 and X6 are separately named models.

sources.title: Writer API changelog
sources.evidence: April 28, 2025 explicitly renames Palmyra X 004 to Palmyra X4; this establishes identity across the old and new names, not a new-model release date.

sources.title: Introducing actions with Palmyra X4
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27: the October 9, 2024 formal release announcement describes synthetic-data training, function tools and 128k context, but gives no nominal parameter count or named base checkpoint. Generic reasoning claims and the RAG tool thought process do not document a separate model thinking mode. Full text was accessible through the web reader.

sources.title: Bringing AI superpowers to Slack
sources.evidence: September 16, 2024 dated article explicitly offers building apps with Palmyra X4 and deploying them through Slack. This predates the formal October announcement. The currently served article uses the later X4 name, so retrospective edits are possible; exact initial rollout day is not established.

sources.title: What is new at Writer: September and October 2024 entries
sources.evidence: September 17, 2024 Slack entry identifies Palmyra X 004 as an available model for general mode. October 9 separately announces the model and tool-calling update. Read directly from the served support page; it does not provide immutable historical revisions.

sources.title: Writer Palmyra X4 model specification and invocation schema
sources.evidence: Exact writer.palmyra-x4-v1:0 entry explicitly states 128,000 context and text modality. April 28, 2025 is the Bedrock availability date. Request schema documents ordinary sampling and response format; example reasoning_content is null, which alone does not prove a lack of reasoning support.

sources.title: Writer chat-completion API
sources.evidence: Current OpenAPI schema supports palmyra-x4 and function tool definitions. No X4-specific reasoning mode or reasoning-effort control is documented. Shared token-usage fields are not proof that this exact model supports an exposed thinking channel.

sources.title: Writer Platform Services Agreement, sections 2 and 5
sources.evidence: Developer terms grant limited non-exclusive, non-transferable platform access and restrict reproduction, modification and downloading components. Used with the documented commercial API distribution to support a descriptive proprietary classification. Indexed full terms were accessible.

sources.title: Palmyra X 004 dummy repository metadata
sources.evidence: Re-fetched October 27 without authentication: the explicitly dummy repository remains at ed07a15b022086795955124c6a03062cda602764, with LlamaForCausalLM and 72,706,859,008 stored BF16 elements. Files are manually gated. This is a count of the named dummy artifact; the metadata does not affirm that it represents the released X4 model size.

sources.title: Palmyra Creative model card
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27 and fetched the raw card: Creative explicitly states that it is fine-tuned from Palmyra-X-004 and advertises nominal 122B. This is positive lineage evidence and would normally support nominal inheritance if the process preserved model structure. The separately found CTO interview in s25 describes merging and slicing multiple models during Creative development, so the fine-tune label alone does not establish unchanged size here.

sources.title: Palmyra X 4.3 model card
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27: the separately named Palmyra-X-4.3-73B card identifies Writer/Palmyra-X-004 as base_model and retains the Writer Open Model License. The 73B name is a valid nominal size for X4.3. This later descendant does not by itself disprove the specific Creative-to-X004 count inference; it also does not directly specify the X4 count or license.

sources.title: Writer-submitted 2025 transparency disclosure
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27: the developer-submitted disclosure identifies Palmyra X5 as its subject; indicator 35 reports 456B and a hybrid Transformer/MoE architecture, and indicator 37 says X5 is not derived from another model. These are X5 disclosures, not X4 specifications.

sources.title: Synthetic data: Busting the myths holding back enterprise AI progress
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27: the January 13, 2025 exact-X4 training discussion describes synthetic-data training and function calling, but supplies no total/active count or sized base-model lineage.

sources.title: Introducing self-evolving models
sources.evidence: November 2024 research describes experimental Transformer modifications and says they were not publicly available. It does not identify X4 as that architecture; no transfer is made.

sources.title: Writing in the Margins: Writer GTC presentation
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27: the Writer GTC presentation includes palmyra-x-004 inference examples and chunked-context processing, but no parameter-count disclosure. The presentation concerns inference patterns rather than a full X4 model specification.

sources.title: Palmyra X 004 launch interview
sources.evidence: Reopened indexed article: approximately 150B is reported attribution; Alshikh directly states only above 100B. Direct page returned 403.

sources.title: Exact named X004 repository
sources.evidence: Rechecked October 27: both the exact named repository metadata API and raw README returned HTTP 401 without authentication. No credentials, approval requests, or weight downloads were attempted.

sources.title: NVIDIA Palmyra X 004 card route
sources.evidence: Rechecked October 27: the exact NVIDIA card route was inaccessible through the web reader. The earlier generic application shell and this failed recheck provide no model count.

sources.title: Writer staff explanation of Palmyra Creative and X004 lineage
sources.publisher: Writer organization account wassemgtk, via Hugging Face
sources.evidence: The October 28, 2024 Writer reply explicitly identifies Creative as a fine-tune of X004 and X004 as a Writer-retrained Llama-based model. Its following statement about greater depth has an ambiguous antecedent and comparison: it does not establish that Creative has more layers than X004. This source supports Transformer architecture and the fine-tune relationship, but is not used as proof of a Creative-versus-X004 structural change.

sources.title: Writer-submitted May 2024 Palmyra X transparency report
sources.evidence: The earlier report says the largest Palmyra model is dense with 72B parameters. Its May 2024 scope predates the September 2024 X004 availability established elsewhere in this report, and it does not identify X004; this nominal size cannot be assigned to X4.

sources.title: May Habib interview: Palmyra X004 training and model family
sources.publisher: Writer CEO May Habib, interview transcript hosted by The MAD Podcast
sources.evidence: November 21, 2024 interview, 23:30–25:28: the CEO discusses X004 training cost, then the core X-series and domain models collectively. She illustrates their large scale with 100B and 200B and describes Transformer improvements, but does not assign either size to X004 or disclose an active count. Family-level examples are not an exact-model nominal specification.

sources.title: Writer Palmyra-X-004 32K vendor Marketplace listing
sources.evidence: The Writer-sold listing identifies an X004 32K deployment and describes its capabilities and inference options. No total/active parameter count or sized base checkpoint is provided. Its deployment-specific context value is not substituted for the documented X4 API context.

sources.title: Palmyra Creative pinned model configuration
sources.evidence: Fetched the public configuration without weights: LlamaForCausalLM, 140 hidden layers, hidden size 8192, intermediate size 28672, 64 attention heads, 8 key/value heads and vocabulary size 128256. These are Creative specifications. Without an X004 configuration they do not identify a difference relative to X004, and no such difference is assumed from this configuration alone.

sources.title: Palmyra Creative repository metadata and nominal-size corroboration
sources.evidence: Re-fetched metadata for revision 11756c451193aa998c6365b1a51a4bbc1918ca06, last modified October 16, 2024. The card names Writer/Palmyra-X-004 as base_model and the public safetensors metadata totals 121,892,970,496 F16 elements, corroborating Creative nominal 122B. No weight shards were downloaded. This confirms the descendant size rather than measuring X004.

sources.title: Writer CTO interview on Creative model merging and layer slicing
sources.publisher: Writer CTO Waseem Al Shikh, direct interview published by Digiday
sources.evidence: In the January 3, 2025 direct Q&A on Creative development, Al Shikh says three separately trained models were combined by merging and interleaving their layers, including slicing the models. This is positive evidence of model/layer restructuring beyond an ordinary unchanged-structure fine-tune. He gives neither the input sizes nor a count-preservation rule, and does not identify an X004 total. The interview does not prove that Creative and X004 have different sizes; it prevents treating ordinary fine-tuning size preservation as established for this relationship.

sources.title: Writer Palmyra Creative launch announcement
sources.evidence: The official Creative release describes a specialized model available through Writer and NVIDIA NIM. It provides neither a comparison of Creative and X004 network shapes nor an X004 parameter count, and therefore does not resolve the model-merging issue raised by the CTO interview.

name.note: Current official name; formerly Palmyra X 004.

developer.note: Exact developer documentation and release announcement.

family.note: X4 is part of the documented Palmyra family.

release_date.note: Month precision is an inference from September 16–17 first-party availability statements, which predate the October 9 formal launch. Exact first public day is unresolved and the current pages may contain retrospective naming edits. April 2025 was a rename and later Bedrock distribution, not the initial release.

open_weights.note: Documented production access is commercial hosted service. Publicly listed dummy weights and separately named descendants do not establish an open production X4 checkpoint. Exact repository contents could not be inspected.

license.note: Descriptive hosted-model classification supported by restricted service rights. The separately released X4.3 checkpoint license is not transferred.

parameters_b.note: Reassessed nominal 122B inheritance from the explicitly documented Creative fine-tune of X004. Creative's developer card and metadata support its 122B size, and the ambiguous greater-depth reply does not establish a Creative-versus-X004 change. However, the CTO directly describes Creative development as merging three models, shuffling layers and slicing models. That documented restructuring defeats the usual assumption of an uncomplicated size-preserving fine-tune; input sizes and its count effect are unstated. This does not prove a different X004 size, but leaves 122B an unresolved candidate rather than a verified X4 specification. X4.3's later 73B alone is not a rebuttal. No independent developer-published nominal X4 total was found; the null does not demand a tensor census.

active_parameters_b.note: Rechecked alongside the Creative-lineage reassessment. Exact-X4 sources and the CTO's development discussion supply no separate active-parameter count or counting convention. Creative's dense Llama configuration describes the descendant; its total and the broad X004 Transformer classification are not used to invent an X4 per-token active count.

architecture.note: The October 28, 2024 Writer organization reply explicitly identifies X004 as a retrained Llama-based model, supporting Transformer classification. Dummy LlamaForCausalLM metadata and the CEO discussion corroborate this. The reply does not unambiguously compare Creative's depth with X004; neither the descendant configuration nor the later discussion of Creative merging is used to claim an exact X004 depth, routing layout or sized Llama base.

context_window.note: Native docs state 128k; AWS explicitly gives 128,000. Provider input/output limits are separate and are not summed to replace the advertised context.

modalities.note: Exact X4 serving specification is text-to-text. Family-level multimodal marketing and X5 image support are not assigned to X4.

reasoning.note: Clear baseline true: general reasoning ability, RAG thought-process explanations and a nullable shared response field do not establish a dedicated X4 thinking mode. No such exact-model API control or behavior was verified; this is not proof of inability.

tool_call.note: Exact launch code and API schema document function definitions and tool-call outputs.

description.value: Enterprise language model for workflow automation, coding, data analysis, and tool use
description.note: Baseline description matches documented use cases without benchmark superiority claims.

patch.notes: Palmyra X 004 was renamed Palmyra X4 in April 2025. September 2024 availability is inferred from dated Writer Slack announcements; October 9 is the formal launch, and the exact first day remains unresolved because current pages may contain later edits. The October 27 parameter re-audit verifies Transformer architecture from Writer's explicit Llama-based X004 statement. Creative's nominal 122B and its explicit fine-tune relationship were reassessed as potential size-inheritance evidence; the greater-depth wording does not itself establish a change relative to X004. A separate direct CTO interview does document Creative construction through merging three models and shuffling/slicing layers, so an ordinary size-preserving fine-tune cannot be assumed. It does not establish that the sizes differ either. The X4 total therefore remains unverified and its active count undisclosed; neither dummy metadata nor X4.3's later size resolves this. Generic reasoning claims do not verify a dedicated thinking mode. Writer schedules X4 deprecation for December 14, 2026.

summary: October 27 parameter re-audit verifies X004's Transformer architecture and rechecks nominal 122B inheritance from Creative's explicit fine-tune lineage. Creative's card, pinned 140-layer configuration and metadata confirm that descendant specification. The greater-depth staff reply is ambiguous and is not evidence of expansion relative to X004. Newly examined direct CTO testimony instead documents Creative-specific multi-model merging and layer slicing, leaving the size-preservation assumption unresolved. Retained explicit null patches for X4 total and active parameters, without requiring an exact tensor census or treating X4.3's later size as proof against Creative lineage. All unrelated audited fields are preserved.
